findings.source_quote: καὶ ὁμῶς ἔμαθον καὶ τῷ πυλῶνι ἐπέστην
findings.english_quote: I nevertheless learned where it was and came to the gateway.
findings.issue: The concessive relation expressed by “nevertheless” is not adequately supported here. The supplied ὁμῶς ordinarily expresses likeness or co-occurrence, including “together” or “at the same time.” The surrounding clauses describe requesting and obtaining information without stating an intervening obstacle. The note's appeal to “all the same” does not distinguish equal manner from the concessive English idiom. This concerns interpretation of the verified reading, not an OCR defect.
findings.suggested_revision: Compare a co-occurrence rendering such as “I learned where it was and at the same time came to the gateway.” If retaining “nevertheless,” substantiate a concessive use of the supplied ὁμῶς and explain the contextual contrast. Preserve the printed form rather than silently substituting ὅμως.

findings.source_quote: ὅτι πάντα τὰ κατὰ σὲ καλὰ ὄντα ἀψευδῶς ἀντέβαλλον
findings.english_quote: for I truthfully related all the good things about you
findings.issue: The English restricts Barnabas's report to the category of good things. The predicate-position καλὰ ὄντα also supports the materially broader claim that everything concerning Clement was represented as good. The draft neither preserves that predication transparently nor explains its restrictive interpretation.
findings.suggested_revision: Compare “for I truthfully described everything about you as good.” If retaining the restrictive rendering, document its grammatical and contextual rationale and preserve the broader predicative interpretation as an alternative. This ambiguity does not require source verification or automatically block publication.

findings.english_quote: in honor of the God who truly is
findings.issue: ὄντως qualifies θεοῦ as genuinely or really God. The draft instead makes bare existence the explicit predicate, and its rationale incorrectly treats an existential force as inherent in the adverb. Mentioning “the true God” as an alternative does not establish the chosen existential wording.
findings.suggested_revision: Use “in honor of the real God,” “in honor of the true God,” or “in honor of the one who truly is God.” Revise the lexical note to explain genuineness rather than claiming that ὄντως itself supplies a separate assertion of existence.

findings.english_quote: (by which I mean a resolve for good words)
findings.issue: The draft converts the participial explanation λέγων into an explicit first-person utterance inside Peter's quotation. In the supplied construction, λέγων can attach to Peter as the subject of the narrative ἔφη, producing a narrator's explanation of what Peter meant. The notes discuss the meaning of προαίρεσιν λόγων καλῶν but do not disclose this change in presentation or the alternative speaker attachment.
findings.suggested_revision: Use a speaker-neutral parenthesis such as “(meaning an inclination toward good discourses),” or present “he meant an inclination toward good discourses” as a narrative aside outside Peter's quotation. Preserve the viable lexical alternatives already identified and explain the attachment of λέγων.
